templates.name: (No template – free text)
ssl – Fragments of sessile serrated lesion.
templates.diagnosis:
Fragments of sessile serrated lesion.
Negative for dysplasia and malignancy.
templates.micro: Sections show fragments of a serrated polyp composed of colonic crypts with serrated luminal contours.  Several of the crypts have a horizontal orientation at the mucosal base.  The findings support a sessile serrated lesion.  No dysplasia or malignancy is identified.

templates.name: hp – Hyperplastic polyp.
templates.diagnosis: Hyperplastic polyp.
templates.micro: Sections show polypoid fragments of colonic mucosa with focal areas showing serration of the surface epithelium. No dysplasia or malignancy is identified.

templates.name: ta – Tubular adenoma.
templates.diagnosis:
Tubular adenoma.
Negative for high-grade dysplasia and malignancy.
templates.micro: Sections show fragments of adenomatous polyp with tubular features. There is no evidence of high-grade dysplasia or malignancy.

templates.name: tas – Fragments of tubular adenoma(s).
templates.diagnosis:
Fragments of tubular adenoma(s).
Negative for high-grade dysplasia and malignancy.
templates.micro: Sections show fragments of adenomatous polyp with tubular features. There is no evidence of high-grade dysplasia or malignancy.

templates.name: sslta – Fragments of sessile serrated lesion, negative for dysplasia and malig
templates.diagnosis:
Fragments of sessile serrated lesion, negative for dysplasia and malignancy.
Fragments of tubular adenoma, negative for high-grade dysplasia and malignancy.
templates.micro: Sections show fragments of a serrated polyp composed of colonic crypts with serrated luminal contours.  Few of the crypts have a horizontal orientation at the mucosal base.  The findings support a sessile serrated lesion.  No dysplasia or malignancy is identified.  In addition, there are fragments of adenomatous polyp with tubular features.  There is no evidence of high-grade dysplasia or malignancy.

templates.name: randomcolon – Benign colonic mucosa with no significant pathologic abnormalities.
templates.diagnosis:
Benign colonic mucosa with no significant pathologic abnormalities.
Negative for microscopic colitis, dysplasia, and malignancy.
templates.micro: Sections show fragments of benign colonic mucosa with a small reactive lymphoid aggregate noted within the lamina propria.  There is no evidence of acute colitis, microscopic colitis (lymphocytic and collagenous), dysplasia, or malignancy identified.

templates.name: food – Polypoid fragments of food material.
templates.diagnosis: Polypoid fragments of food material.
templates.micro: Sections show only fragments of food material with no colonic tissue present for evaluation.

templates.name: benignpolyp – Polypoid fragment of benign colonic mucosa with no significant patholo
templates.diagnosis:
Polypoid fragment of benign colonic mucosa with no significant pathologic abnormalities.
Negative for dysplasia and malignancy.
templates.micro: Sections show a polypoid fragment of benign colonic mucosa with an intact surface epithelium without evidence of erosion or ulceration. The lamina propria appears to be of a normal cellularity.  No prominent superficial serration is appreciated, and no dysplastic crypts are present. No diagnostic features of dysplasia or malignancy are identified. Multiple step-level sections are examined.

templates.name: duodenum – Duodenal mucosa with no significant pathologic abnormalities.
templates.diagnosis: Duodenal mucosa with no significant pathologic abnormalities.
templates.micro: Sections shows strips of benign duodenum mucosa that demonstrate normal villous architecture.  There is no increase in intraepithelial lymphocytes.  No evidence of dysplasia or malignancy is identified.

templates.name: peptic – Chronic (peptic-type) duodenitis.
templates.diagnosis: Chronic (peptic-type) duodenitis.
templates.micro: Sections show benign small intestinal mucosa with a normal villous architecture without evidence of definite blunting or crypt hyperplasia. Foci of foveolar metaplasia are noted along the surface. No increase in intraepithelial lymphocytes is appreciated. Brunner gland hyperplasia is seen. The lamina propria shows chronic inflammation. No diagnostic features of dysplasia or malignancy are identified.

templates.name: acutepeptic – Acute and chronic (peptic-type) duodenitis, ulcerated.
templates.diagnosis: Acute and chronic (peptic-type) duodenitis, ulcerated.
templates.micro: Sections show fragments of benign small intestinal mucosa with normal villous architecture without evidence of blunting or crypt hyperplasia.  There are multiple foci of foveolar metaplasia noted along the surface.  There is an increase in chronic inflammation within the lamina propria.   There is also foci of acute inflammation within the glandular epithelium.  Brunner gland hyperplasia is seen.  There are also multiple fragments of fibrinous material with acute inflammation consistent with extensive ulceration.  There is no evidence of dysplasia or malignancy identified.

templates.name: gastritis – Chronic gastritis.
templates.diagnosis:
Chronic gastritis.
Negative for Helicobacter pylori organisms by immunohistochemistry.
Negative for intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia, and malignancy.
templates.micro: Sections show benign gastric mucosa without evidence of ulceration or intestinal metaplasia. The lamina propria contains scattered chronic inflammatory cells. No marked acute inflammation is seen. No Helicobacter pylori organisms are present on a routine H&E stain and by immunohistochemical staining, performed and interpreted in conjunction with appropriate and working positive control material. No features of dysplasia or malignancy are identified.

templates.name: hpgastritis – Helicobacter pylori-associated gastritis.
templates.diagnosis:
Helicobacter pylori-associated gastritis.
Negative for intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia, and malignancy.
templates.micro: Sections show benign gastric mucosa without evidence of ulceration or intestinal metaplasia. The lamina propria is expanded by chronic inflammatory cells. Few neutrophils are seen in surface and gland epithelium. There are reactive epithelial changes.  Helicobacter pylori organisms are identified on routine H&E stain and by immunohistochemical staining, performed and interpreted in conjunction with appropriate and working positive control material. No features of dysplasia or malignancy are identified.

templates.name: stomachhp – Hyperplastic polyp.
templates.diagnosis: Hyperplastic polyp.
templates.micro: Sections show polypoid fragments of gastric mucosa with hyperplastic foveolar epithelium with elongation of the crypts, branching, some with dilated lumens.  There is fibromuscular hyperplasia. No Helicobacter pylori organisms are present on a routine H&E stain and by immunohistochemical staining, performed and interpreted in conjunction with appropriate and working positive control material. No intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia, or malignancy is identified.

templates.name: stomachfgp – Fundic gland polyp.
templates.diagnosis: Fundic gland polyp.
templates.micro: Sections show fragments of polypoid oxyntic mucosa containing architecturally irregular and cystically dilated fundic glands.  No intestinal metaplasia is seen.  No Helicobacter pylori organisms are identified on routine H&E stain. No features of dysplasia or malignancy are identified.

templates.name: reactiveeso – Squamous mucosa with reactive epithelial changes.
templates.diagnosis:
Squamous mucosa with reactive epithelial changes.
Negative for dysplasia or malignancy.
templates.micro: Sections show benign-appearing and mildly spongiotic, stratified squamous epithelium without evidence of ulceration. Mild basal cell hyperplasia is appreciated. No prominent intraepithelial eosinophilic or neutrophilic infiltrates are noted. No glandular epithelium is present.  No features of dysplasia or malignancy are identified.

templates.name: tinl – Small bowel mucosa with no significant pathologic abnormalities.
templates.diagnosis: Small bowel mucosa with no significant pathologic abnormalities.
templates.micro: Sections show fragments of small bowel mucosa with no significant pathologic abnormalities.  There is a small reactive lymphoid aggregate identified.  There is no evidence of dysplasia or malignancy.

templates.name: tinonspecific – Fragments of ileal mucosa with prominent lymphoid aggregates and minim
templates.diagnosis:
Fragments of ileal mucosa with prominent lymphoid aggregates and minimal nonspecific ileitis.
Negative for dysplasia and malignancy.
templates.micro: Sections show fragments of small bowel mucosa with mostly preserved villous architecture and chronic inflammation with prominent lymphoid aggregates within the lamina propria and rare neutrophilic inflammation.  Cells with viral cytopathic effects are not identified on H&E-stained sections.  No granulomas are identified.  There is no evidence of dysplasia or malignancy.

templates.name: ccc – Chronic cholecystitis and cholelithiasis.
templates.diagnosis:
Chronic cholecystitis and cholelithiasis.
One periductal lymph node, negative for malignancy (0/1).
templates.micro: Sections show a thickened gallbladder wall with evidence of mucosal protrusion into the muscular layer.  Scattered chronic inflammatory cells are present. No diagnostic features of dysplasia or malignancy are identified. One benign periductal lymph node is identified that is negative for malignancy.

templates.name: acutechole – Acute and chronic cholecystitis with cholelithiasis.
templates.diagnosis: Acute and chronic cholecystitis with cholelithiasis.
templates.micro: Sections show a thickened gallbladder wall.  The mucosal surface is mostly eroded and associated with a chronic inflammatory cell infiltrate that includes lymphocytes and plasma cells.  Scattered neutrophils are also seen within the gallbladder wall.  No dysplasia or malignancy are identified.

templates.name: cholesterolosis – Chronic cholecystitis and cholesterolosis with cholelithiasis.
templates.diagnosis: Chronic cholecystitis and cholesterolosis with cholelithiasis.
templates.micro: Sections show a benign gallbladder with occasional foamy histiocytes in the lamina propria. There is slight fibrosis with a chronic inflammatory infiltrate in the background.  The mucosal epithelium shows no significant cytologic atypia or dysplasia.  The specimen is negative for malignancy.

templates.name: appendicitis – Acute appendicitis and periappendicitis.
templates.diagnosis: Acute appendicitis and periappendicitis.
templates.micro: Sections of the appendix show an acute inflammatory infiltrate involving the appendiceal mucosa, muscular wall, and periappendiceal tissue.  There is no evidence of appendiceal perforation.  There is no evidence of atypia or malignancy identified.

templates.name: perfappendix – Marked acute appendicitis with periappendicitis and transmural inflamm
templates.diagnosis: Marked acute appendicitis with periappendicitis and transmural inflammation/defect, suggestive of perforation.
templates.micro: Sections of the appendix demonstrate mucosal erosion with marked fibrinopurulent exudate. The inflammation extends through the wall of the appendix and into the periappendiceal soft tissue.  Areas of transmural inflammation with defects are noted, suggestive of perforation. There is no evidence of atypia or malignancy identified.

templates.name: ischemicbowel – Benign small bowel with features consistent with ischemic enteritis.
templates.diagnosis:
Benign small bowel with features consistent with ischemic enteritis.
Resection margins are viable.
Negative for dysplasia and malignancy.
templates.micro: Sections show small bowel with areas of transmural acute and chronic inflammation, including areas of mucosal necrosis, ulceration, and hemorrhage. There is acute serositis and serosal adhesions.  Ischemic-type changes are also seen.  The surgical resection margins are viable.  No evidence of dysplasia or malignancy is identified.

templates.name: negascites – Negative for malignant cells.
templates.diagnosis: Negative for malignant cells.
templates.micro: Review of the ThinPrep preparation reveals benign appearing mesothelial cells,  histiocytes, and mixed inflammatory cells.  The cell block shows similar findings.  There are no cytologic features of malignancy identified.

templates.name: bph – Benign prostatic gland tissue with glandular and stromal hyperplasia.
templates.specimen: PROSTATE CHIPS, TRANSURETHRAL RESECTION OF PROSTATE
templates.diagnosis:
Benign prostatic gland tissue with glandular and stromal hyperplasia.
Acute and chronic prostatitis.
Negative for atypia and malignancy.
templates.micro: Sections of the prostate show benign prostatic parenchyma. The prostate tissue is notable for glandular and stromal hyperplasia along with patchy acute and chronic inflammation. No atypia or malignancy is identified.

templates.name: endo – Features compatible with endometriosis.
templates.diagnosis: Features compatible with endometriosis.
templates.micro: Sections show fibrous tissue with chronic inflammation, focal areas suggestive of endometrial stroma, and scattered hemosiderin deposition, suggestive of endometriosis.  There is no diagnostic evidence of malignancy identified.

templates.name: suggendo – Endometriosis.
templates.diagnosis: Endometriosis.
templates.micro: Sections show fibrous tissue with chronic inflammation and endometriosis.  There is no evidence of malignancy.

templates.name: noendo – Fibrous tissue with hemosiderin and mixed inflammation; see microscopi
templates.diagnosis:
Fibrous tissue with hemosiderin and mixed inflammation; see microscopic description.
No diagnostic endometriosis present.
templates.micro: Sections show fibrous tissue with mixed inflammation and hemosiderin.  There is no diagnostic endometriosis identified. These findings can be seen in the setting of endometriosis. No malignancy is identified.

templates.name: melanoma – Involved by melanoma.
templates.diagnosis: Involved by melanoma.
templates.micro: Sections show fragments of fibrous tissue involved by malignant cells composed of intermediate to large sized cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm. There are areas of necrosis seen. Focal areas of lymphoid tissue is seen. Immunohistochemical stains are performed and interpreted in conjunction with appropriate working positive control material. The tumor cells are positive for S100, SOX10, and synaptophysin. They are negative for pancytokeratin AE1/AE3, CAM5.2, p40, CK7, CK20, GATA3, GCDFP-15, CDX2, PAX8, TTF1, NKX3.1, p16, and CD45.

templates.name: tonsilSCC – Invasive squamous cell carcinoma, HPV-associated.
templates.diagnosis: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma, HPV-associated.
templates.micro: Sections show fragments of an invasive squamous cell carcinoma. The tumor cells show variably abundant pink to basophilic cytoplasm with nuclear hyperchromasia. The tissues are fragmented and extent of invasion cannot be further determined. Immunohistochemical staining is performed and interpreted in conjunction with appropriate and working positive control material.  The tumor cells show diffuse (>90%) block positivity for p16.

templates.name: benigncx – Benign squamous mucosa.
templates.diagnosis:
Benign squamous mucosa.
Negative for dysplasia and malignancy.
templates.micro: Sections show fragments of benign cervical squamous mucosa with no evidence of atypia, dysplasia, or malignancy.

templates.name: benigncxtx – Cervical transformation zone with acute and chronic inflammation and r
templates.diagnosis: Cervical transformation zone with acute and chronic inflammation and reactive epithelial changes.
templates.micro: Sections show benign cervical transformation zone mucosa with acute and chronic inflammation and reactive cellular changes.  No dysplasia or malignancy is identified.

templates.name: cxpolyp – Benign endocervical polyp.
templates.diagnosis: Benign endocervical polyp.
templates.micro: Sections show sampling of polypoid cervical tissue containing a fibrovascular core exhibiting acute and chronic inflammation.  The polyp is covered by endocervical glandular epithelium and areas of squamous metaplasia and reactive epithelial changes.  There are also scant fragments of background benign secretory phase endometrium. No atypia, hyperplasia, dysplasia or malignancy is identified.

templates.name: embsec – Benign secretory endometrium.
templates.diagnosis:
Benign secretory endometrium.
Negative for hyperplasia and malignancy.
templates.micro: Sections of the endometrium show benign secretory phase endometrium with no evidence of hyperplasia or malignancy.

templates.name: embprolif – Benign proliferative endometrium.
templates.diagnosis: Benign proliferative endometrium.
templates.micro: Sections show sampling of benign endometrial tissue with overall gland:stromal ratios of less than one. The glands are tubular and mitotically active in unremarkable stroma.  No polyp, hyperplasia, atypia, or malignancy is identified.

templates.name: embprolhormone – Benign proliferative endometrium with glandular and stromal changes su
templates.diagnosis:
Benign proliferative endometrium with glandular and stromal changes suggestive of exogenous hormone effect.
Negative for hyperplasia and malignancy.
templates.micro: Sections show sampling of benign proliferative phase endometrial tissue with areas of stromal decidualization.  No atypia, hyperplasia, polyp or malignancy is present.

templates.name: prolifbreak – Benign proliferative endometrium with breakdown.
templates.diagnosis: Benign proliferative endometrium with breakdown.
templates.micro: Sections show sampling of endometrial tissue exhibiting glands with overall gland: stromal ratio of less than one.  The endometrium shows mostly benign proliferative phase endometrium.  There are areas of stromal collapse consistent with breakdown.  No hyperplasia or malignancy is present.

templates.name: subleio – Fragments of submucosal leiomyoma/leiomyomata.
templates.diagnosis:
Fragments of submucosal leiomyoma/leiomyomata.
Negative for atypia and malignancy.
templates.micro: Sections show fragments of smooth muscle which consists of a cellular proliferation in a background of occasional hyalinization.  There is no significant cytologic atypia, atypical mitoses, or necrosis.  Some fragments of smooth muscle are surfaced by endometrial tissue, which shows benign inactive endometrium.  No atypia, hyperplasia, or malignancy are identified.

templates.name: stripsinactive – Superficial strips of benign inactive endometrium.
templates.diagnosis:
Superficial strips of benign inactive endometrium.
Negative for hyperplasia and malignancy.
templates.micro: Sections show superficial strips of benign inactive endometrium (>10 strips present). No diagnostic features of hyperplasia, atypia, and malignancy are identified.

templates.name: inactivebreakdown – Benign inactive endometrium with stromal breakdown.
templates.diagnosis: Benign inactive endometrium with stromal breakdown.
templates.micro: Sections show sampling of fragmented benign endometrial tissue with inactive glands in a background of stromal collapse and hemorrhage.  There is no atypia, hyperplasia, or malignancy.

templates.name: endopolyp – Benign endometrial polyp.
templates.diagnosis: Benign endometrial polyp.
templates.micro: Sections show polypoid fragments of endometrium with fibrous stroma and thick-walled vessels, compatible with endometrial polyp.  No diagnostic features of hyperplasia, atypia, and malignancy are identified.

templates.name: endomyo – Fragments of endometrium suggestive of benign endometrial polyp in a b
templates.diagnosis:
Fragments of endometrium suggestive of benign endometrial polyp in a background of benign secretory endometrium.
Fragments of myometrial tissue.
Negative for hyperplasia and malignancy.
templates.micro: Sections show fragments of fibrous stroma with occasional clustering of vessels, compatible with benign endometrial polyp. The background shows fragments of benign secretory phase endometrium. Fragments of myometrial tissue are also present, which may represent fragments of submucosal leiomyoma versus contiguous myometrium. There is no evidence of atypia, hyperplasia, or malignancy.

templates.name: lsil – Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (CIN 1).
templates.diagnosis: Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (CIN 1).
templates.micro: Sections show cervical transformation zone mucosa exhibiting disordered maturation with nuclear enlargement, nuclear membrane irregularities, hyperchromasia and low overall nuclear: cytoplasmic ratios. The dysmaturational changes and mitotic activity are confined to the lower portion of the epithelium.  The background mucosa shows acute and chronic inflammation. There are no definitive diagnostic features of high grade dysplasia. No malignancy is identified.

templates.name: cin2 – High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (CIN 2).
templates.diagnosis: High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (CIN 2).
templates.micro: Sections show cervical mucosa exhibiting disordered maturation with cytologic atypia and dysmaturational changes involving the basal and mid-portion of the squamous epithelium.  No invasive carcinoma is identified.

templates.name: cin2-3 – High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL)/CIN 2-3.
templates.diagnosis: High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL)/CIN 2-3.
templates.micro: Sections show cervix at transformation zone with areas of low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion. Additionally, there are areas with dysmaturation, loss of polarity, mitotic activity extending into the upper half of the epithelium. There is no evidence of invasive carcinoma. Immunohistochemical staining is performed and interpreted in conjunction with appropriate and working positive control material. Immunostaining shows strong, full thickness staining for P16, confirming the diagnosis.

templates.name: ecchsil – Detached fragments of high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL
templates.diagnosis: Detached fragments of high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL)/CIN 3.
templates.micro: Sections show small detached fragments of squamous mucosa with dysmaturation, loss of polarity, mitotic activity extending into the upper half of the epithelium. Immunohistochemical staining is performed and interpreted in conjunction with appropriate and working positive control material. Immunostaining shows strong, block positive full thickness staining for p16, confirming the diagnosis. The Ki67 proliferation index also shows increased proliferation into the upper half of the epithelium.

templates.name: hyst – UTERINE WEIGHT: 160 g
templates.specimen: UTERUS WITH BILATERAL FALLOPIAN TUBES AND OVARIES, HYSTERECTOMY AND BILATERAL SALPINGO-OOPHORECTOMY
templates.diagnosis:
UTERINE WEIGHT: 160 g
CERVIX: Parakeratosis; chronic cervicitis; negative for dysplasia and malignancy
ENDOMETRIUM: Benign inactive endometrium; negative for hyperplasia and malignancy
MYOMETRIUM: Superficial adenomyosis; multiple leiomyomata, intramural and subserosal; negative for atypia and malignancy
SEROSA: No significant abnormalities
RIGHT FALLOPIAN TUBE: Benign paratubal cysts
RIGHT OVARY: Cortical inclusion cysts
LEFT FALLOPIAN TUBE: Benign paratubal cysts
LEFT OVARY: Cortical inclusion cysts
templates.micro: Sections of the serosa show no significant abnormalities.  The cervix shows parakeratosis and chronic cervicitis with no evidence of dysplasia or malignancy. The endometrium shows benign inactive phase endometrium.  There is no evidence of hyperplasia or malignancy.  Sections of the myometrium show superficial adenomyosis and multiple leiomyomata that are intramural and subserosal with no evidence of atypia or malignancy.  The bilateral fallopian tubes show benign paratubal cysts.  There is no significant tubal inflammation or evidence of malignancy.  The bilateral ovaries show multiple cortical inclusion cysts and are negative for malignancy.

templates.name: ptc – Papillary thyroid carcinoma, classic variant; see Synoptic Table below
templates.diagnosis: Papillary thyroid carcinoma, classic variant; see Synoptic Table below.
templates.synText:
THYROID GLAND

TUMOR
Tumor Focality:  Unifocal
Tumor Characteristics
Tumor Site:  Right lobe
Tumor Size:  Greatest Dimension (Centimeters) - 2.1 x 2 x 1.4 cm
Histologic Tumor Types and Subtypes:  Papillary carcinoma, classic subtype
Tumor Proliferative Activity
Mitotic Rate:  Less than 3 mitoses per 2mm2
Tumor Necrosis:  Not identified
Angioinvasion (vascular invasion):  Not identified
Lymphatic Invasion:  Not identified
Extrathyroidal Extension:  Not identified
Margin Status:  All margins negative for carcinoma
REGIONAL LYMPH NODES
Regional Lymph Node Status:  Not applicable (no regional lymph nodes submitted or found)
DISTANT METASTASIS
Distant Site(s) Involved:  Cannot be determined
pTNM CLASSIFICATION (AJCC 8th Edition)
Reporting of pT, pN, and (when applicable) pM categories is based on information available to the pathologist at the time the report is issued. As per the AJCC (Chapter 1, 8th Ed.) it is the managing physician's responsibility to establish the final pathologic stage based upon all pertinent information, including but potentially not limited to this pathology report.
pT Category:  pT2
pN Category:  pN not assigned (no nodes submitted or found)
templates.micro: Sections of the thyroid lobe demonstrate a dominant nodule, consistent with papillary thyroid carcinoma, classic variant.  The carcinoma is confined to the thyroid gland.  No extrathyroidal extension is identified. No lymphatic, angioinvasion, or perineural invasion is identified.

templates.name: niftp – Non-invasive follicular thyroid neoplasm with papillary-like nuclear f
templates.diagnosis: Non-invasive follicular thyroid neoplasm with papillary-like nuclear features (NIFTP), 8 mm, excised; see Comment.
templates.micro: Sections show thyroid parenchyma that contains a well-circumscribed, encapsulated follicular lesion containing variably sized follicles and patchy areas showing nuclear features of papillary thyroid carcinoma, including nuclear enlargement/crowding, grooves, and pseudoinclusions.  Notably, there is lack of psammomatous calcifications, papillary architecture, tumor necrosis, infiltrative border, and capsular invasion. The lesion measures 8 mm in greatest dimension.  Taken together, these findings are consistent with non-invasive follicular thyroid neoplasm with papillary-like nuclear features (NIFTP).  The background thyroid parenchyma is notable for prominent hyperplastic changes with multiple hyperplastic nodules characterized by variably-sized and cystically dilated follicles with abundant colloid.
templates.comment: The right thyroid gland contains a well-circumscribed, encapsulated follicular lesion containing variably sized follicles with patchy areas showing nuclear features of papillary thyroid carcinoma. Given the lack of psammomatous calcifications, papillary architecture, tumor necrosis, infiltrative border, and capsular invasion, these findings are consistent with non-invasive follicular thyroid neoplasm with papillary-like nuclear features (NIFTP).

templates.name: idcdcislump – Invasive ductal carcinoma and ductal carcinoma in situ; see synoptic t
templates.diagnosis: Invasive ductal carcinoma and ductal carcinoma in situ; see synoptic table below.
templates.micro: Sections show breast parenchyma involved by a solitary focus of invasive ductal carcinoma, which measures 26 mm in greatest dimension and confined to the breast parenchyma.  The carcinoma cells are intermediate in size with occasionally conspicuous nucleoli.  Approximately 12 mitotic figures are seen in 10 high-power fields, and demonstrate histologic features consistent with a Nottingham score of 7/9 (grade 2).  There is no definitive evidence of lymphovascular invasion.  Areas of intermediate-grade ductal carcinoma in situ carcinoma is present with solid patterns.  Central comedo-type necrosis is also present.  The foci of DCIS are located both within and adjacent to the invasive carcinoma. The invasive and in situ carcinoma is most closely seen 2 mm from the posterior (black inked) and 5 mm from the anterior (blue inked) margins. The DCIS is most closely seen 6 mm from the posterior (black inked) margin.  The background breast parenchyma is notable for biopsy-related changes.

templates.name: negLN – Two lymph nodes, negative for malignancy (0/2)
templates.diagnosis: Two lymph nodes, negative for malignancy (0/2)
templates.micro: The intraoperative touch preparations are reviewed concurrently with the permanent sections; they show concordant findings. Sections show two benign lymph nodes that are negative for malignancy.  Immunohistochemical stains are performed on all blocks and interpreted in the context of appropriate control material.  Stains for pancytokeratin AE1/AE3 are performed and confirm the above findings.

templates.name: posLN – Metastatic carcinoma in four of four lymph nodes (4/4)
templates.diagnosis:
Metastatic carcinoma in four of four lymph nodes (4/4)
Largest tumor deposit measures 9 mm
Extranodal extension not identified
templates.micro: Sections show a total of four lymph nodes, all of which are positive for metastatic carcinoma.  There are two lymph nodes in slide C1, with tumor deposits measuring 5 mm and 6 mm in greatest dimension. The largest tumor deposit measures of 9 mm in greatest dimension is seen in the lymph node in slide C2. Extranodal extension is not identified. The lymph node in slides C3-C4 shows a 2 mm tumor deposit with no definitive extranodal extension identified.

templates.name: idclump – Invasive ductal carcinoma; see synoptic table below
templates.diagnosis: Invasive ductal carcinoma; see synoptic table below
templates.micro: Sections show a single focus of invasive ductal carcinoma, which measures 19 mm in greatest dimension.  The tumor demonstrate histologic features consistent with a Nottingham score of 8/9 (grade 3).  Lymphovascular invasion is identified.  There is no evidence of ductal carcinoma in situ.  The surgical margins are negative, and the tumor most closely approaches the posterior (black inked) margin at a distance of 3 mm.  The background breast parenchyma is notable for biopsy site changes.

templates.name: dcislump – Ductal carcinoma in situ, high grade; see synoptic table below.
templates.diagnosis: Ductal carcinoma in situ, high grade; see synoptic table below.
templates.micro: Sections show multiple discontiguous foci of DCIS associated with prior biopsy site changes.  In slide 7, the DCIS spans 1 mm in greatest dimension. The foci of DCIS show predominantly high nuclear grade with a predominantly solid growth pattern. There is also atypical ductal hyperplasia (ADH) in the background. DCIS is located 1 mm from the posterior (black inked) margin.  The background breast parenchyma shows fibrocystic changes including columnar cell changes, duct ectasia, and microcysts.  Biopsy site changes are noted.  There is no invasive carcinoma identified.

templates.name: idcbx – Invasive ductal carcinoma; see synoptic table below
templates.specimen: XX BREAST, XX O’CLOCK, XX CM FROM NIPPLE, BIOPSY
templates.diagnosis: Invasive ductal carcinoma; see synoptic table below
templates.synText:
INVASIVE CARCINOMA OF THE BREAST: Biopsy

TUMOR
Histologic Type:  Invasive ductal carcinoma
Glandular (Acinar) / Tubular Differentiation:  Score 3
Nuclear Pleomorphism:  Score 2
Mitotic Rate:  Score 1
Overall Grade:  Grade 2
Ductal Carcinoma In Situ (DCIS):  Not identified
Comment(s):  Biomarkers to be reported separately in an addendum.
templates.micro: Sections show cores of breast parenchyma involved by invasive ductal carcinoma, composed of irregular tumor cells arranged in tubules with surrounding fibrosis. The carcinoma cells are intermediate in size with occasional and conspicuous nucleoli.  Less than one mitotic figure is seen in 10 high power fields. Taken together the findings represent a Nottingham score of 5/9, consistent with histologic grade 1.  In greatest extent, the largest focus of tumor measures 5 mm.  There is no definitive evidence of lymphovascular invasion identified. Immunohistochemical stains are performed and interpreted in the context of appropriate control material.  The tumor cells are positive for pancytokeratin AE1/AE3, E-cadherin, CK7, and GCDFP-15. They are negative for GATA3, CK20, TTF1, CDX2, and PAX8.

templates.name: idcbx2 – Invasive ductal carcinoma; see synoptic table below
templates.specimen: XX BREAST MASS, XX CM MASS, XX O’CLOCK, BIOPSY
templates.diagnosis: Invasive ductal carcinoma; see synoptic table below
templates.synText:
INVASIVE CARCINOMA OF THE BREAST: Biopsy

TUMOR
Histologic Type:  Invasive ductal carcinoma

templates.name: LNneg – Lymph node – no monoclonal B-cells
templates.fullText:
Results:
- Mixed lymphocytes without monoclonal B-cells or aberrant T-cell antigen expression.

Interpretation:
Flow cytometry was performed to evaluate for evidence of an abnormal lymphoid population. The lymphoid gate (low SSC/FSC) shows a heterogeneous population of lymphoid cells with a predominance of T-cells and smaller numbers of B-cells. T-cells show a mixture of CD4 and CD8 subtypes, with the former predominating. Neither aberrant antigen expression among lymphoid cells nor a monoclonal B-cell population is detected.

There is no evidence of a clonal B-cell population. Flow cytometry may not detect classical Hodgkin lymphoma, some T-cell neoplasms or non-hematolymphoid malignancies. Correlation with any morphologic data is recommended.

Interpreted by Jyoti Kumar, M.D.

templates.name: LNscant – Lymph node – scant cellularity
templates.fullText:
Results:
- Scant cellularity with few mixed lymphocytes
- No monoclonal B-cell population

Interpretation:
Flow cytometry was performed to evaluate for evidence of an abnormal lymphoid population. Overall specimen lymphoid cellularity is scant, with few events in the expected region of mature lymphocytes. The cells in the usual lymphoid gate (low SSC/FSC) show a T-cell predominance and smaller numbers of B-cells. Neither aberrant antigen expression among lymphoid cells nor a monoclonal B-cell population is detected.

Most events show scatter properties consistent with non-specific debris and/or blood.

There is no evidence of a clonal B-cell population in this limited cellularity sample. Flow cytometry may not detect classical Hodgkin lymphoma, some T-cell neoplasms or non-hematolymphoid malignancies. Correlation with any morphologic data is recommended.

Interpreted by Jyoti Kumar, M.D.

No viable monoclonal B-cell population is detected.

While there is no evidence of a clonal B-cell population, the sample shows limited cellularity and is mostly comprised of debris. There are very few events on the forward-vs-side scatter plot that lie in the expected region of lymphoid cells. The events in this region express CD2 or CD5, consistent with T-cells. CD19-positive B-cells are nearly absent, and do not include an abnormal population. Most events show scatter properties consistent with debris and/or sub-viable cells.

templates.name: PBnegflow – Peripheral blood – negative
templates.fullText:
Results:
- No appreciable CD34-positive blast population
- Mixed lymphocytes without monoclonal B-cells or aberrant T-cell antigen expression

Interpretation: Flow cytometry was performed on the peripheral blood to evaluate for evidence of an abnormal lymphoid population. The lymphoid gate (CD45+, low SSC/FSC) shows a heterogeneous population of lymphoid cells with a predominance of T-cells and smaller numbers of B-cells and NK-cells. T-cells show a mixture of CD4 and CD8 subtypes, with the former predominating. Neither aberrant antigen expression among lymphoid cells nor a monoclonal B-cell population is detected.

The monocyte/large lymphocyte gate (CD45+, moderate SSC/FSC) shows predominantly CD33 bright cells consistent with monocytes. Monocytes do not show aberrant antigen expression.

Most analyzed events are mature granulocytes which show high side-scatter and no aberrancies of analyzed antigens. Gating on blasts (mod CD45+/low SSC) shows no appreciable increase in CD34-positive events.

There is no evidence of a clonal B-cell population or circulating blasts. Flow cytometry may not detect chronic myeloproliferative disorders or some T-cell neoplasms. Correlation with any morphologic data is recommended.

Interpreted by Jyoti Kumar, M.D.

templates.fullText:
BONE MARROW, BIOPSY, CLOT SECTION AND ASPIRATE:
- HISTOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS:  Normocellular marrow with maturing trilineage hematopoiesis, mild eosinophilia, and no increase in blasts; see Comment.
   - IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY:  Performed; see microscopic description.
   - IRON STAIN:  Decreased quantity and distribution of stainable storage iron
   - RETICULIN STAIN:  Focal mild increase in marrow fibrosis (focal MF-1)
- ADEQUACY OF SPECIMEN:  Adequate

   - FISH STUDIES:  The result is within normal limits for the chronic eosinophilia FISH panel.
- MOLECULAR STUDIES:  No BCR/ABL1 mRNA transcripts were detected.

PERIPHERAL BLOOD:
- Hypochromic, microcytic red cells 
- Mild prominence of eosinophils 
- No significant abnormalities of platelets  

The patient is a XX-year-old female with a reported history of persistent eosinophilia for two years. The current CBC shows eosinophilia.

Morphologic and immunophenotypic examination of the bone marrow reveals a normocellular marrow with maturing trilineage hematopoiesis and eosinophilia both in the peripheral blood and bone marrow. There is no abnormal increase in blasts or overt dysplasia. Most known causes of eosinophilia are secondary/reactive and include allergy/atopy, infection, immune/autoimmune disease, vasculidities, solid tumor malignancies, and drug effect, and these causes should be specifically clinically excluded. The specimen was submitted for ancillary studies for further evaluation of primary causes of eosinophilia, but cytogenetic studies were normal, while FISH and molecular analyses were negative, making a primary neoplastic hematolymphoid process unlikely. Clinical correlation is recommended.

No increase in schistocytes or red cells with oxidative injury is seen. Occasional tear-drop forms are seen. Occasional elliptocytes are present. Leukocytes are normal in number, consisting predominantly of segmented neutrophils with fewer numbers of lymphocytes and monocytes. There is an absolute increase in eosinophils that show normal morphology. No circulating malignant blasts or dysplastic changes are seen. Platelets are normal in number and morphology.

BONE MARROW, ASPIRATE AND TOUCH PREPARATION: The aspirate slides contain cellular marrow particles. Myeloid precursors appear adequate in number with full spectrum maturation. Few eosinophils are noted without morphologic abnormalities. Erythroid precursors are adequate in number with full spectrum maturation. Too few megakaryocytes are present for evaluation. Immunohistochemistry, special stains, and/or in-situ hybridization is performed (with working controls) in conjunction with flow cytometry immunophenotyping. This is deemed necessary as the flow cytometry sample yielded negative/non-contributory findings with respect to the process in question.

Interpretation: Flow cytometry was performed on the bone marrow to characterize blasts. Gating on blasts (mod CD45+/low SSC) demonstrates few CD34-positive events that represent 0.5% of total CD45+ events. These events express the myeloid markers CD117 and CD13, consistent with maturing myeloid progenitors. Some events in this region express CD19 and CD10 and show scatter properties consistent with hematogones.    - FISH STUDIES:  No assay specific abnormalities detected by AML FISH panel
- MOLECULAR STUDIES:  MayoComplete Oncoheme NGS panel showed 2 pathogenic mutations:
   1) CEBPA: Chr19(GRCh37):g.33793258dup; c.68dup; p.His24Alafs*84 (48%)
   2) CEBPA: Chr19(GRCh37):g.33792384_33792386dup; c.937_939dup; p.Lys313dup (48%)

- 63% circulating blasts
- Normochromic, normocytic anemia 
- Marked thrombocytopenia without spurious platelet clumps   

The overall findings are consistent with acute myeloid leukemia with CEBPA mutation. The co-existence of the N-terminal (p.1−120) frameshift/nonsense mutation(s) and C-terminal bZIP (p.278−358) in-frame indel/missense mutation(s) identified is consistent with the reported classical pattern of biallelic CEBPA. Classical biallelic (double) mutations in intermediate risk AML have been associated with a more favorable prognosis than CEBPA-unmutated or CEBPA-single mutated cases (Wouters et al., 2009, 19171880; Green et al., 2010, 20439648; Dofour et al., 2010, 20038735 and Fasan et al., 2014, 24056881). However, more recent studies have demonstrated similarly favorable outcome in bZIP-mutated AML irrespective of double or single CEBPA-mutated status, particularly associated with bZIP in-frame mutations (Tarlock et al., 2021, 33951732; Taube et al., 2021, 34320176; Wakita et al, 2021, 34448807).

BONE MARROW, BIOPSY, CLOT SECTION AND ASPIRATE:

   - Hypercellular marrow with decreased background trilineage maturing hematopoiesis, and 81.5% blasts by aspirate differential count. 
   - IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY:  Performed; see microscopic description

   - KARYOTYPE:  Normal Male Karyotype - 46,XY[20]
   - FISH STUDIES:  No assay specific abnormalities detected by AML FISH panel
- MOLECULAR STUDIES:  MayoComplete Oncoheme NGS panel showed two pathogenic mutations:
1) FLT3: Chr13(GRCh37):g.28608282_28608287del; NM_004119.2(FLT3):c.1770_1775del; p.Tyr591_Val592del (7%)
2) NPM1: Chr5(GRCh37):g.170837544_170837547dup; NM_002520.6(NPM1):c.860_863dup; p.Trp288Cysfs*12 (40%)

PERIPHERAL BLOOD:
- Normochromic, macrocytic anemia 
- Leukocytosis with 78% circulating blasts 
- Marked thrombocytopenia without spurious platelet clumps  

The overall findings are consistent with acute myeloid leukemia. Cytogenetic studies showed a normal karyotype and molecular studies identified an NPM1 and FLT3 mutation. The FLT3 mutation is an in-frame deletion overlaps with the binding and switch motifs of the juxtamembrane domain (Griffith et al., 2004, 14759363; Berenstein, 2015, 26309392). Although this variant is not a FLT3-internal tandem duplication (FLT3-ITD) or a FLT3-tyrosine kinase domain (FLT3-TKD) alteration involving codons D835/I836, and has not been previously described, in-frame deletions have been recurrently reported as somatic mutations in acute myeloid leukemia. Furthermore, in vitro functional data of other juxtamembrane domain deletions demonstrates constitutive phosphorylation of downstream targets, growth factor independent proliferation of cells, and reduced apoptosis, which was suggested to be a result of disruption of the protein's autoinhibitory conformation (Chatain et al., 2015, 26012842). Therefore, this variant is considered likely pathogenic. The overall findings are consistent with acute myeloid leukemia with NPM1 mutation.

The patient is a XX-year-old female with reported monoclonal gammopathy. The patient's
current CBC is notable for normocytic anemia.

Given the presence of both a kappa-restricted B cell population and a kappa-restricted
plasma cell population detected by flow cytometry, these two populations likely
represent manifestations of the same neoplasm given the shared light chain restriction.
These findings are most compatible with low-grade B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic
differentiation, such as lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma which is favored, although marginal
zone lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation is another possibility. Finally, a
separate, unrelated plasma cell neoplasm (e.g. myeloma) is difficult to completely
exclude, and clinical correlation to assess for myeloma-associated clinical
manifestations (e.g. lytic bone lesions) is suggested. Correlation with pending
cytogenetic and molecular studies, including evaluation for a MYD88 mutation, is
recommended. These ancillary studies have been initiated and the results will be
incorporated into the final report.

consistent with lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma given the presence of a MYD88 L265P
alteration identified by molecular analysis.

Flow cytometry was performed on the bone marrow to evaluate for evidence of an
abnormal lymphoid and plasma cell population. The lymphoid gate (CD45+, low

dim), but not CD5, CD10 or hairy-cell leukemia antigens (CD103 or CD11c). Surface

represents approximately 7.3% of all CD45+ events. The remainder of lymphoid events

bright, moderate SSC) are enumerated at 0.1%. These plasma cells show cytoplasmic
kappa-light chain restriction expressing CD19, and lack expression of CD45, CD56,
and CD20. Note, flow cytometry will underestimate the true percentage of plasma
cells in the marrow, due to selective loss during processing.

CD33 bright cells consistent with monocytes. Monocytes do not show aberrant antigen
expression.

side-scatter and no aberrancies of analyzed antigens. Gating on blasts (mod
CD45+/low SSC) shows few CD34-positive myeloid progenitors accounting for 0.5% of
total events.

with marginal zone lymphoma or lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma. There is also a clonal
plasma cell population. The abnormal B cell population has the same light chain
restriction as the abnormal plasma cell population seen. Given the similar light
chain restriction, these two populations likely represent manifestations of the
same neoplasm, but correlation with any morphologic data as well as serum
electrophoresis can help differentiate among these possibilities.

The patient is a XX-year-old male with a previous diagnosis of chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL).

The bone marrow is markedly hypercellular with decreased trilineage maturing hematopoiesis and shows extensive involvement by the patient's previously diagnosed CLL/SLL. FISH is positive for a deletion of chromosome 13 including 13q14/DLEU1 (91.5% of nuclei). Deletion of the long arm of chromosome 13q is the most common genetic alteration detected in patients with B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia (B-CLL) by FISH analysis and is seen in ~50 to 60% of patients. Isolated deletion 13q14.3 is considered a favorable prognostic indicator in the absence of adverse genetic markers.

templates.name: FL3A – Classic follicular lymphoma, grade 3A.
templates.fullText:
LYMPH NODE, XX, BIOPSY:
-  Classic follicular lymphoma, grade 3A.
-  Flow Cytometry: XX.

Sections show fragments of tissue containing a nodular atypical lymphoid proliferation composed of a mixture of centrocytes and centroblasts. A majority of nodules have a predominance of centroblasts (greater than 15 per high-power field); however, there are scattered centrocytes admixed and no diffuse areas composed entirely of centroblasts are seen. Immunohistochemical stains are performed on block A2 and interpreted in the context of appropriately reactive control material. The neoplastic cells express CD20, CD10, BCL2, and BCL6. They are negative for CD3, CD5, CD43, MUM1, CD30, and C-MYC. The Ki-67 proliferation index is 20-30% overall and increased up to 80% in some neoplastic follicles. CD21 highlights expanded follicular dendritic cell meshworks that are associated with the neoplastic follicles. Kappa and lambda light chain protein stains show high background staining and are difficult to interpret. EBV by in situ hybridization (EBER) is negative.

Results:  
- Lambda-restricted CD10+ B-cell population, 29%

Interpretation:  Flow cytometry was performed to evaluate for evidence of an abnormal lymphoid population. The lymphoid gate (CD45+, low SSC/FSC) shows a lambda-restricted population of CD19+ B-cells expressing uniform CD20 and CD10, but not CD5. Surface immunoglobulin expression is moderate in intensity. Overall, this population represents approximately 29% of all CD45+ events and shows relatively small size by forward-scatter. The remainder of lymphoid events corresponds to a mixed population of CD4 and CD8 T-cells, which do not show antigenic aberrancies. Fewer polyclonal B-cells are also noted, which lack CD10.

There is a clonal B-cell population which shows an immunophenotype that can be seen most often with lymphomas of follicle center origin, such as follicular lymphoma. Flow cytometry is not an optimal method to assess cell size, however, and the phenotype does not exclude the possibility of a large B-cell lymphoma or Burkitt lymphoma. Correlation with morphologic data is recommended.

COLON, MASS, BIOPSY:
- Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma).

Sections show multiple fragments of colonic mucosa with dense lymphocytic infiltrates in the lamina propria comprised of mostly small sized lymphocytes with irregular nuclear contours, inconspicuous nucleoli, and scant cytoplasm. The grossly identified 6.7 cm appendix mass, on microscopy, show appendix involved by an atypical nodular lymphoid proliferation composed of predominantly small to intermediate sized cells with condensed chromatin, round to monocytoid nuclei, and scant to moderate amounts of pale cytoplasm. A background of increased plasma cells are noted. Scattered larger cells are noted but not forming sheets. Scattered residual follicles with reactive germinal centers are also present.  Immunohistochemical stains are performed and interpreted in conjunction with appropriate and working positive control material. CD20 labels increased small sized lymphocytes. The interfollicular B-cells are negative for CD5, CD10, and BCL6. Coexpression of BCL2 and CD43 is difficult to evaluate, but favored to show variable expression on a subset of the B-cells. Background germinal centers are highlighted by BCL6 and CD10, which are appropriately negative for BCL2. The Ki67 proliferation index appears low within the neoplastic B-cells and appropriately high in the germinal centers. CD138 labels the plasma cells. Kappa and lambda light chain protein stains show high background staining and are difficult to interpret. Kappa and lambda by in situ hybridization show kappa predominant plasma cells. The plasma cells appear to lack co-expression of CD56 and CD117 based on the distribution of staining as compared to CD138. The plasma cells express predominantly IgG, fewer expressing IgA, and rare forms positive for IgM. IgG stains plasma cells with less than 5% cells highlighted by IgG4.CD21 highlights follicular dendritic cell meshworks. CD3 labels few numbers of admixed small T-cells.

Molecular studies were positive for a B-cell gene rearrangement in IGH (NeoGenomics XX).

templates.name: hypercellularPTH – Hypercellular parathyroid tissue
templates.diagnosis: Hypercellular parathyroid tissue (XX g).
templates.micro: Sections demonstrate a hypercellular parathyroid gland.  The glandular parenchyma demonstrates a follicular growth pattern.  There are mature chief cells and oxyphil cells. The cells show no significant cytologic atypia or increased mitotic activity.  There is no evidence of necrosis.  No significant adipose tissue is present in the glandular parenchyma. Taken together, the findings are compatible with a parathyroid adenoma; however, correlation with clinical and laboratory findings is required.

templates.name: nonspecificduodenitis – Focal nonspecific chronic duodenitis
templates.diagnosis: Focal nonspecific chronic duodenitis; see microscopic description.
templates.micro: Sections show fragments of small bowel mucosa, the majority of which shows normal villous architecture without an increase in intraepithelial lymphocytes.  One focus shows blunted villous architecture, with reactive change.  This focus also does not show an increase in intraepithelial lymphocytes, but there is increased density of the lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate within the lamina propria.  These findings are not diagnostic of celiac disease, and are most consistent with focal nonspecific chronic duodenitis, but correlation with clinical and serologic findings is recommended.  No acute activity is seen and there is no dysplasia or malignancy.  No pathogenic organisms are present.

templates.name: liverfibrosis – Liver biopsy: advanced fibrosis (stage 3-4), mild portal inflammation, mild siderosis

Advanced fibrosis (stage 3-4); see Comment.

templates.comment: The biopsy demonstrates advanced fibrosis (stage 3-4 of 4), approaching cirrhosis. The etiology of the fibrosis is not evident on histologic examination. Portal inflammatory infiltrates are mild and composed predominantly of lymphocytes with occasional histiocytes. Interface activity, prominent plasma cell-rich inflammation, hepatocyte rosetting, and emperipolesis are not identified. There is no significant steatosis, balloon cell change, Mallory-Denk bodies, or features of steatohepatitis. Mild ductular proliferation, focal cholestatic change, and focal copper deposition are present but may be secondary to advanced fibrosis. If the patient has received corticosteroid therapy, the degree of inflammatory activity may be attenuated. Correlation with clinical findings, serologic studies, and treatment history is recommended.
templates.micro: Sections show an adequate quantity of portal tract cross-sections for evaluation.  Portal inflammatory infiltrates are mild and composed predominantly of lymphocytes with occasional histiocytes.  There is mild bile ductular proliferation.  Mild cholestatic change is seen. A diastase pre-digested PAS stain shows scattered ceroid-laden macrophages and reveals no diastase-resistant globules of alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency. A trichrome stain shows stage 3-4 fibrosis. A reticulin stain shows no significant cell plate atrophy. A copper stain shows focal copper deposition.  An immunohistochemical stain for CK7 is also performed and evaluated with appropriately reacting controls.  CK7 demonstrates a mild ductular proliferation.

templates.comment: The overall findings are mild and nonspecific and may represent changes secondary to an extrahepatic process. The liver biopsy also shows mild centrilobular sinusoidal dilatation, which can be seen in a minority of drug-induced liver injury, but is commonly associated with nodular regenerative hyperplasia or outflow dysfunction in the setting of cardiac conditions.  Clinical correlation is recommended.

In some areas, there is zonal sinusoidal dilatation with mild cell plate atrophy.  Special stains are performed and evaluated with appropriately reactive controls. A Prussian blue stain shows no increase in Kupffer iron storage. A diastase pre-digested PAS stain shows scattered ceroid-laden macrophages and reveals no diastase-resistant globules of alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency. A trichrome stain shows focal/minimal sinusoidal fibrosis. A reticulin stain highlights mild cell plate atrophy. A copper stain is negative. The patient is a XX-year-old female with a reported history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma status post R-CHOP now with pancytopenia.

The overall findings are consistent with acute myeloid leukemia, which may be therapy-related given the patient's history. Cytogenetic studies demonstrated a MLLT3/MLL(KMT2A) fusion resulting in t(9;11)(p22;q23). Molecular analyses identified a pathogenic mutation in XX. In the context of the identified genetic abnormalities, these findings are consistent with acute myeloid leukemia with KMT2A rearrangement.

PERIPHERAL BLOOD: The red cells are decreased in number and are normochromic and normocytic with mild anisopoikilocytosis and increased polychromasia. No increase in schistocytes or red cells with oxidative injury is seen. Leukocytes are decreased in number, consisting of an absolute reduction in neutrophils and lymphocytes, with few monocytes. No circulating malignant blasts or dysplastic changes are seen. Platelets are markedly decreased in number and mostly normal in morphology. No platelet clumps are seen.

BONE MARROW, ASPIRATE AND TOUCH PREPARATION: The aspirate slides contain adequate cellular marrow particles and show increased blasts that are intermediate in size with moderate amounts of cytoplasm, fine nuclear chromatin, and prominent nucleoli that occasionally vacuolated cytoplasm. Background trilineage maturing hematopoiesis is markedly reduced. No lymphoid infiltrates are identified and no large atypical lymphocytes are seen. There is no increase in plasma cells. The touch preparation slides show a similar cellularity. Iron stains on the aspirate slides (with appropriately working controls) show adequate storage iron. No ring sideroblasts are seen.

Interpretation: Flow cytometry was performed on the bone marrow to characterize blasts. Gating on blasts (mod CD45+/low SSC) demonstrates an abnormal population that represents 88% of total CD45+ events. The blasts express CD117 and show myeloid differentiation with CD13, CD33, HLA-DR. They express CD64 and CD15. They are negative for CD34, CD56, and CD14. Evaluation of cytoplasmic markers shows  expression of MPO (partial), but not TdT, cCD79a or cCD3.
Maturing granulocytes are proportionally reduced, show high side-scatter and no aberrancies of analyzed antigens.
The monocyte/large lymphocyte gate (CD45+, moderate SSC/FSC) shows predominantly CD33 bright cells consistent with monocytes. Monocytes do not show aberrant antigen expression.
The lymphoid gate (strong CD45+, low SSC) shows a heterogeneous population of lymphocytes with a predominance of T-cells and smaller numbers of B-cells and NK-cells. Neither aberrant antigen expression among lymphoid cells nor a monoclonal B-cell population is detected.
There is an increase in myeloid blasts, consistent with acute myeloid leukemia.
